cells.tense: You are holding many knowings at once, and the shape in them is plain to you.
cells.act: put the frame on the table before anyone asks
cells.ask: Before the next meeting, write the frame in a few plain lines and hand it over first. Say the shape once, out loud, then stop there and see what they do with it.
cells.core:
You're carrying more than one knowing at a time, and they aren't fighting each other. Patterns come up clean for you — you can see how something works under its surface, and what you see usually turns out right. People bring you the tangled case because next to you it sorts itself out.
What keeps that working is plain: put the frame on the table before anyone asks for it. Hand over the structure early, your own words, without needing agreement. It's yours to state — you saw it first. That's what keeps the whole thing load-bearing instead of something you quietly carry by yourself.
cells.sheetLine: You see the shape. Say it before anyone asks.
cells.verb: Holding many knowings at once — and seeing the pattern under them
cells.place: Where the pattern shows itself apart from any one case

cells.tense: The pattern is plain to you, and you are already braced for a case that has not arrived.
cells.act: face one way for three days
cells.ask: Pick one direction from what you actually want, not from the argument, and hold it for three days. Turn down whatever arrives that would pull you off the heading.
cells.core:
Seeing how things work isn't the problem — you do that well. The trouble is you're doing it ahead of time: the conversation coming next week, the thing that might go sideways, the person who may need the pattern. You're inside all of them already, before any have arrived. From where you sit, the future looks like more of the same, so you load up for it early.
Holding one heading is what settles it — not seeing less. Choose the direction you actually want, not the one that wins the argument, and stay with it for three days. Let the new cases wait their turn. Being right was not the risk. Being in six places at once is. Keep the one heading and the rest will hold.

cells.tense: The seeing is still yours, and it has stopped going anywhere.
cells.act: choose one connection and flow with it
cells.ask: Pick one person you already trust to see what you see — not a project, just one — and tell them the pattern you've been noticing, in your own words. Then be quiet and give them the floor.
cells.core:
The pattern under things still shows up for you the way it did. What's changed is where it goes: lately it stays with you, kept private, rather than being said to anyone. You've been holding it at the edge instead of handing it across, and it has drawn in to something only you know about.
More certainty won't move it. One person will — someone who already sees the way you do — and one telling: what you've been noticing, said plainly, not sold. Then give them the floor. You don't have to defend the perception. It needs a place to land, and one person is enough of that.
cells.sheetLine: You still see it. Say it to one person.
cells.verb: Holding many knowings at once — and seeing the pattern under them
cells.place: Where the pattern shows itself apart from any one case

cells.tense: You read the situation accurately and file it under instinct rather than your own judgment.
cells.act: act on the private sense of what is right
cells.ask: When your own sense of what's fair points somewhere, act on it — no witness, no announcement. Afterwards, mark to yourself that the call was yours.
cells.core:
The read you're running is yours to claim — the accuracy has been there the whole time. It gets filed as instinct, or as just how things are, or as what anyone would notice. Meanwhile that read has been quietly setting the terms: what gets said, what gets held back, where the lines fall.
What returns it is small and unwitnessed. When your own sense of what's fair points somewhere, act on it — no credit, no account, no one watching. That's the private compass doing its real work, and it has done that work steadily; you just haven't been counting it as yours. Do one thing it asks and treat that as the start.
cells.sheetLine: The read is yours. You've been filing it as instinct.

attempts.check: The record supports the seat's mechanism (pattern seen beneath content, and what that seeing costs) but not the claim that the person has been right about what they see — in Too Little I lean on 'landed and didn't hold,' which is inference, not fact. A reader could reasonably say their knowing never landed anywhere because nothing was ever offered to it, not because they stayed at the door. Every ask survives being wrong: a closed loop, one heading held for three days, one stream joined, one small debt returned each teaches the person their own shape regardless of my read. The sentence that serves me more than them is the 'many windows' figure; I've cut it.
